entry.title: Inside 0.37.0, our biggest update yet
entry.summary: A rebuilt interface, a tactical map, photo mode, optional player accounts, bots that respect your line of fire, one-life Bomb rounds and a long list of fixes from your reports. Here is what changed, why, and how we tested it.

entry.title: Inside 0.36.0, the update you can hear
entry.summary: Voice chat, team pings, bots that read the map, a full audio overhaul and an optional 128 updates per second. This is the long version: what changed, why we built it the way we did, how it was tested, and what is still to come.

entry.title: A new look, from the loading screen to the kill feed
entry.summary: Loading screens that teach the map, a tactical map, a match-end podium, photo mode, HDR output, clearer error screens and a launcher you can drive with a controller. Here is what is coming and how it was built.

entry.title: Every map, in 3D, in your browser
entry.summary: The six map pages now carry a 3D model of the real map that you can turn, cut open and study before your first round, and every update gets a page of its own.

entry.title: Finding new players without tracking anyone
entry.summary: TrueCombat: Platinum is about to go public on more platforms than ever. To learn which of them actually bring players, the site now counts visits and downloads the same way it counts devlog readers: no cookies, no outside companies, and nothing that leads back to you.

entry.title: Inside 0.35.0, our biggest update yet
entry.summary: Easy Anti-Cheat with no sign-up, a launcher rebuilt from scratch, player stats from every verified match and the bulk of the playtest fixes. This is the long version: what changed, why we built it the way we did, how it was tested, and what did not make it.

entry.title: Every fight on the record
entry.summary: Player profiles are about to get a lot deeper, and unranked servers count too. Here is what we track, and the rules that keep every number honest.

entry.title: The road ahead, in full
entry.summary: The next two updates are planned, and so is the work behind them. A rebuilt movement core, a match record that powers replays and coaching, bots that have to look and listen like you do, pickup games on Discord and more. This is the long version, with how each piece works and why we are building it this way.

entry.title: Counting readers without tracking anyone
entry.summary: Every devlog post now ends with a star rating, and we can finally see which posts people read. Here is how we built that without cookies, without analytics and without storing anything that points back to you.

entry.title: What we are working on next
entry.summary: With 0.34.0 out, here is an open look at the work lined up behind it: better online play, Discord pickups, one-click joining, and a set of new features built on a shared match record. Plans, not promises.

entry.title: Free means free: how support works
entry.summary: TrueCombat: Platinum now has a support page and a Ko-fi. Why we added it, where the money goes, and the rules we set for ourselves so that supporting never changes how the game plays.

entry.title: What the playtests told us
entry.summary: Our latest community playtests turned up a clear list of problems, led by gunplay. A large batch of fixes is lined up for the next patch. Here is everything we found, the order we will fix it in, and how it fits with the rest of the work coming up.

entry.title: The official servers now run on Linux
entry.summary: Both official servers have moved to a native Linux build of the 0.34.0 server. What that means for your matches, why we did it, and how we made sure we could undo it in seconds.

entry.title: New light for old maps
entry.summary: The Ultra preset brings modern lighting, real surface materials and sun shadows to every map on DirectX 12. Here is how we built it without changing how TC:E plays.

entry.title: Teaching bots to play like people
entry.summary: Bots that never miss are no fun, and bots that ignore the objective are worse. This is how we test every change to Platinum's bots before it reaches a server.

entry.title: When the test is wrong
entry.summary: Our recoil checks flagged the Desert Eagle as broken. The game was right. Here is how we found out, and why we would rather chase a false alarm than miss a real one.

entry.title: Ten pieces of work, one update
entry.summary: The next update was built by ten separate efforts at the same time. How they came together into one build without stepping on each other, and what the final test gate looked like.

entry.title: What keeps the official servers running
entry.summary: Two official servers, a master list, live leaderboards and this website all run around the clock. Here is what happens behind the scenes when nobody is watching.

entry.title: One small installer, every version
entry.summary: Platinum used to be a zip of almost 800 MB. Now it is a 7 MB installer, a launcher that only downloads what changed, and a button that takes you back to any earlier release.

entry.title: Every shot leaves a mark
entry.summary: Bullet holes, impact sounds, the crack of a near miss and the original weapon animations. How the next update brings back the feel of a TC:E firefight.

entry.title: Match mode, built for clan nights
entry.summary: Clan matches are where TC:E lived. Platinum 0.32 brings a full match flow to every server, with a pause that freezes the whole world.

entry.title: Back to full speed
entry.summary: For months Platinum felt a step slower than the game we remember. The cause turned out to be a single scaling factor, applied in the wrong place.
